# Anchor: schema_proof_format

> Scope: specs/**/*.proofs-*.json, scripts/proof/
> Description: Defines the JSON schema for proof files emitted by test runners, the agnostic and platform-scoped file names, how plugins merge results when re-running tests (write-scoped overwrite, keyed by `(feature, tier, platform, test_file)`), and how `sync_status` discovers the files and reads them to compute rule coverage.

## Rules

- RULE-1: Proof files live in the same directory as their spec and are named `<feature>.proofs-<tier>.json` (platform-agnostic) or `<feature>.proofs-<tier>@<platform-id>.json` (scoped to one platform). Which of the two a result lands in is decided by the test's marker, not by the host (`proof_common` RULE-17)
- RULE-2: The JSON schema has a top-level `tier` string and a `proofs` array; a scoped file also has a top-level `platform` string equal to the id in its name. Each proof entry contains: `feature`, `id`, `rule`, `test_file`, `test_name`, `status`, `tier`, and in a scoped file exactly one more, `platform`, equal to the top-level value
- RULE-3: `status` is either `"pass"` or `"fail"` — no other values
- RULE-4: `tier` values are `"unit"`, `"integration"` and `"e2e"`, and no tier is runner-gated: a tier says what kind of test a proof is, never where it must run. Where a proof must be proved is the spec's `@on(<platform-id>, ...)` tag, and the result of proving it there is a scoped file whose `@` suffix is a registry or family id. A committed `<feature>.proofs-windows.json` from before this rule is read for one release as `unit@windows` with an advisory naming `purlin:init --update`, which renames it; `windows` is not a valid tier in a file name or an entry
- RULE-5: Proof plugins merge on the key `(feature, tier, platform, test_file)`: load the existing file for that `(feature, tier, platform)`, drop the current feature's entries whose `test_file` this run executed or whose `test_file` no longer exists, append the new entries, write the merged result. Within one file the platform is constant, so the file's own merge is unchanged from the three-part key; a run that writes a scoped file leaves the agnostic file and every other platform's file untouched
- RULE-6: Proof files are committed to git — they are project records, not ephemeral build artifacts
- RULE-7: Manual proofs are stamped inline in the spec's `## Proof` section as `@manual(<email>, <date>, <commit_sha>)`, not in proof JSON files
- RULE-8: `sync_status` and `static_checks` discover proof files with one character-identical pattern, `^(.+)\.proofs-([A-Za-z0-9_]+)(?:@([a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*))?\.json$`, grouped by `(feature, tier, platform)` with the same-directory preference. On read every entry is stamped in memory with `platform`: the id from a scoped file name, `None` from an agnostic one. A file whose `@` suffix is outside the id charset matches nothing and is not read. A legacy `<feature>.proofs-windows.json` is read with tier `unit` and platform `windows` on every entry, and `sync_status` prints one advisory per such file naming the file, `read as unit@windows`, the name `purlin:init --update` will give it, and that command; the advisory changes no verdict

## Proof

- PROOF-1 (RULE-1): Create a proof file at `specs/test/foo.proofs-unit.json`; run sync_status; verify it reads the file and associates it with the `foo` spec @integration
- PROOF-2 (RULE-2): Validate every committed proof JSON file against the required fields; verify all 7 fields (`feature`, `id`, `rule`, `test_file`, `test_name`, `status`, `tier`) are present in each proof entry
- PROOF-3 (RULE-3): Create a proof entry with `status: "error"`; run sync_status; verify it is not counted as a passing proof @integration
- PROOF-4 (RULE-4): Scan every committed `*.proofs-*.json` file; verify the tier in each file name is in {unit, integration, e2e}, every `@` suffix matches the platform id charset, and for every non-legacy file the top-level `tier` and `platform` and each entry's `tier` and `platform` equal the file name's. For a legacy `proofs-windows.json`, verify `_read_proofs` returns each of its entries with tier `unit` and platform `windows`. Verify `spec_format.md` documents `@integration`, `@e2e` and `@on(` @integration
- PROOF-5 (RULE-5): Pre-seed a proof file with feature B entries; run the real pytest proof plugin for feature A via subprocess; verify feature B entries are preserved and feature A entries are added. Then pre-seed both `feat_a.proofs-unit@p1.json` and `feat_a.proofs-unit.json` with feature B entries, run the plugin under `PURLIN_PLATFORM=p1` for a feature A marker declaring `platforms=("p1",)`; verify the scoped file keeps B and gains A with `platform: "p1"` on every entry, and the agnostic file is byte-identical to before @integration
- PROOF-6 (RULE-6): Grep `.gitignore` for `*.proofs-*.json`; verify no gitignore rule excludes proof files
- PROOF-7 (RULE-7): Grep `references/formats/proofs_format.md` for `@manual`; verify manual stamp format is `@manual(<email>, <date>, <commit_sha>)`
- PROOF-8 (RULE-5): Pre-seed one tier file with two entries for the same feature recorded against two different `test_file` values; run the real pytest proof plugin for that feature from only one of those files; verify the re-run file's entry is replaced and the other file's entry survives. Repeat with the two entries pre-seeded in `feat_split.proofs-unit@p1.json` and the plugin run under `PURLIN_PLATFORM=p1` with `platforms=("p1",)` markers; verify the same replacement and survival inside the scoped file and that no agnostic file is written @integration
- PROOF-9 (RULE-8): Verify `_proof_file_parts` and `_PROOF_FILE_RE` are source-identical in `purlin_server.py` and `static_checks.py`. In a temp project write `foo.proofs-unit.json`, `foo.proofs-unit@ok-1.json`, `foo.proofs-unit@Bad_Id.json` and `bar.proofs-windows.json`; call `_read_proofs`; verify the agnostic entry reads `platform: None`, the `ok-1` entry reads `platform: "ok-1"`, the `Bad_Id` entry is absent, `bar`'s entry reads tier `unit` platform `windows` and its path is the only item in the legacy list; run `sync_status` and verify it prints the legacy path, `read as unit@windows`, `bar.proofs-unit@windows.json` and `purlin:init --update` while `bar` still reports PASSING or VERIFIED; delete the legacy file and verify the list is empty and the advisory is gone @integration
